question.text: Let circles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> with centres <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> respectively touch each other externally, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>36,7</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mn>20,7</mn></mfenced></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> The coordinates of the centre of a circle passing through the points of contact of circles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> are

solution.text:
The circle which passes through the points of contact of circles C1,C2 & C2,C3 & C3,C1 is the incircle of ΔO1O2O3.

Its centre lies on the angle bisectors of ΔO1O2O3.
Hence, required point is incentre of ΔO1O2O3.
Now, O1O2=56, O2O3=25 & O3O1=39
⇒Ι=56×0+25×-36+39×2056+25+39,25×7+56×-8+39725+56+39
